issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods reference camelCase field names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch in the solution causes compilation errors and is inconsistent with the UML/ problem statement which uses camelCase attribute names. Students comparing solution, template, and problem statement will be confused because the solution as provided does not compile and does not match the specified attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML/problem statement and the rest of the code. Rename the declared fields in the solution to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors — or alternatively update the constructor and all methods to use the declared snake_case names. Preferably use the camelCase names shown in the UML so the template, problem statement, and solution align and the code compiles.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and expected attribute names use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares the fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the rest of the solution code (constructor, getters, setters, methods) references camelCase names. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual attributes creates a direct mapping confusion and will likely cause compilation errors or cognitive load for students trying to map the UML to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align attribute identifiers across artifacts. Rename the declared fields in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to use camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors, and ensure the constructor and all methods reference these exact field names. Prefer camelCase to match the UML and Java conventions.
